verses.text: So I ask: Has God rejected his people? Absolutely not! I'm an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham from the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not rejected his people, whom he knew beforehand. Don't you remember what Scripture says about Elijah, when he appealed to God against Israel?
He said, ‘Lord, they've killed your prophets and torn down your altars. I'm the only one left, and now they're trying to kill me too.’
But what did God tell him? ‘I've kept seven thousand for myself who have never bowed to Baal.’
It's the same now: a remnant has been chosen by grace.
And if it's by grace, it's no longer based on works; otherwise grace wouldn't be grace. If it's based on works, then it's no longer grace; otherwise work wouldn't be work.
So what happened? Israel didn't get what it was seeking. The chosen ones received it, while the rest were hardened,
as Scripture says: ‘God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that can't see and ears that can't hear, to this very day.’
David says: ‘May their table become a trap and a snare, a stumbling block and a fitting punishment.
May their eyes grow dark so they can't see, and may their backs stay bent forever.’
So I ask: Did they stumble in order to fall beyond recovery? Absolutely not! Their trespass brought salvation to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous.
If their trespass brought riches to the world, and their loss brought riches to the Gentiles, how much greater will their full inclusion be!
I'm speaking to you Gentiles. Since I'm an apostle to the Gentiles, I take pride in my ministry,
hoping somehow to make my own people jealous and save some of them.
If their rejection brought the world's reconciliation, what will their acceptance be? Life from the dead!
If the first part of the dough is offered as holy, then the whole batch is holy. If the root is holy, so are the branches.
If some branches were broken off, and you—a wild olive branch—were grafted in among them and now share the rich root of the olive tree,
don't brag over the branches. If you do, remember: you don't support the root; the root supports you.
You may say, ‘Branches were broken off so I could be grafted in.’
That's true. They were broken off because of unbelief, and you stand through faith. Don't get proud; stay humble.
If God didn't spare the natural branches, he won't spare you either.
So look at both God's kindness and his severity: severity toward those who fell, but kindness toward you—if you continue in his kindness. Otherwise, you'll be cut off too.
And if they don't remain in unbelief, they will be grafted in, because God can graft them in again.

If you were cut from a wild olive tree by nature and grafted, against nature, into a cultivated olive tree, how much more readily will these natural branches be grafted back into their own olive tree!
Brothers and sisters, I don't want you to miss this mystery and become conceited: a partial hardening has come over Israel until the full number of Gentiles comes in.
And in this way all Israel will be saved, as Scripture says: ‘The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn godlessness away from Jacob.
And this is my covenant with them when I take away their sins.’
As far as the Good News is concerned, they are enemies for your sake. But as far as God's choice is concerned, they are loved because of the patriarchs.
God's gifts and his call can't be taken back.
Just as you once disobeyed God but now received mercy because of their disobedience,
so they too have now disobeyed, in order that through the mercy shown to you they may also receive mercy.
For God has allowed everyone to be held in disobedience so he can show mercy to everyone.
How deep are God's riches, wisdom, and knowledge! His judgments are beyond searching out, and his ways are beyond tracing.
‘Who has known the Lord's mind? Who has ever been his adviser?’
‘Who has ever given God anything first, so that God should have to repay them?’
Everything comes from him, exists through him, and is for him. Glory to him forever! Amen.
